source.author: lucan
source.text: - Pars maxima turbae Naufraga, iactatis morti obluctata lacertis, Puppis ad auxilium sociae concurrit: at illi Robora cum vetitis prensarent altius ulnis, Nutaretque ratis populo peritura recepto, Impia turba super medios ferit ense lacertos: Brachia linquentes Graia pendentia puppi, A manibus cecidere suis: non amplius undae Sustinuere graves in summo gurgite truncos.
source.text_original: -  Pars maxima turbae / Naufraga, iactatis morti obluctata lacertis, / Puppis ad auxilium sociae concurrit: at illi / Robora cum vetitis prensarent altius ulnis, / Nutaretque ratis populo peritura recepto, / Impia turba super medios ferit ense lacertos: / Brachia linquentes Graia pendentia puppi, / A manibus cecidere suis: non amplius undae / Sustinuere graves in summo gurgite truncos.
source.text_english: Most of the crowd, shipwrecked and struggling against death with their limbs as they were tossed about, rushes from the ship to the aid of their companion: but when they, with their prohibited arms, clung more tightly to the timbers, and the vessel, having received the people, was swaying, doomed to perish, the impious crowd strikes the arms that were in the middle with the sword. The Greeks, leaving their arms hanging from the ship, fell away from their own hands: no longer did the waves support the heavy trunks in the topmost whirlpool.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_original: nec vero Odrysius transtris impenditur Orpheus / aut pontum remo subigit, sed carmine tonsas / ire docet, summo passim ne gurgite pugnent.
reuse.text_english: Nor indeed is Orpheus, son of Odrysius, hung over benches, nor does he drive the sea with an oar; rather, with his song he teaches the shorn oars to go, so that everywhere they do not contend with the top of the wave.
